title: Stabilize inference path selection after scheduler heuristic introduced kernel churn
creator: Marco Li
description: Summary: During a gradual rollout of a scheduler heuristic that biases routing toward shortest-queue replicas, we observed increased kernel-selection churn and KV-cache invalidations for multi-sequence batch workloads. Consequence: p95/p99 tail latency spikes (up to 3x) and 18% sustained throughput drop for workloads with heterogeneous sequence lengths. A subset of Dedicated EU customers experienced degraded call success and elevated error retries. This ticket captures root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and long-term action items to prevent recurrence.

2026-02-27 04:30 UTC: Rollout paused after automated alert from perf-bot (alert id perf-3421).

root_cause: The new scheduler heuristic prioritized shortest-queue routing without incorporating per-request sequence-length features. For heterogeneous batch loads this caused frequent routing oscillation between host paths that prefer different kernel implementations (quantized vs fused-attn kernels), which in turn triggered repeated KV cache invalidations and deoptimized kernel code paths. The observed kernel_switch_rate correlated strongly with elevated p95 and throughput loss.
impact_summary: High: Multiple Dedicated customers in eu-west-1 experienced higher latency and increased retry rates for multi-sequence batching. Internal SLOs for p95 throughput were missed for ~2 hours; billing impact minimal but customer experience impacted.
actions: Immediate: Revert scheduler heuristic from canary and suspend global rollout (done).
Short-term (this sprint): Add a path-stability gating check to the scheduler canary that measures kernel_switch_rate and KV-cache invalidation rate (owner: Aisha).
Short-term: Implement a soft affinity score that includes per-request avg sequence length and model variant compatibility to reduce oscillation (owner: Eric Gomez).
Short-term: Add a circuit-breaker that, if kernel_switch_rate > threshold for a host pair, pins requests to previous stable path for a cooldown period (owner: Priya Nair).
Medium-term: Extend CI perf tests to include synthetic heterogenous-sequence batching scenarios that assert stabilized kernel routing and no >20% increases in kernel_switch_rate (owner: SRE team).
Medium-term: Instrument and export new metrics: kernel_switch_rate, kv_invalidation_count, path_rebind_rate, and expose them in Console per-route panels (owner: Observability team).
Long-term: Update model catalog metadata to surface kernel-compatibility hints and preferred path groups to scheduler (owner: Model Onboarding).
Long-term: Add an offline simulation tool that replays historical traces and predicts churn risk before rollouts (owner: Research).
